# @lidtop/opencode-later

Save the next idea without interrupting the current one. Keep one Later list across your projects, sessions, and terminals, visible in the sidebar, and paste an item into your prompt when it's time. Nothing runs automatically.

[![Watch the Later demo: an idea saved for later by the agent, then reordered and pasted back into the prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackarySantana/opcode/main/docs/images/later-demo.jpg)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c145b7c-be82-4ebe-a735-9e40ba2706d9)

*The 36-second demo uses sample data.*

![Later list alongside an OpenCode session, keeping follow-up ideas visible in the sidebar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackarySantana/opcode/main/docs/images/later-sidebar.png)

![Later manager with four active items, a selected follow-up, and completed history](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ZackarySantana/opcode/main/docs/images/later-manager.png)

## Install

Requires OpenCode **2.2.0 or newer in the 2.x line**.

```sh
opencode plugin add @lidtop/opencode-later
```

Or add it to `plugins` in your global `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` (or `opencode.json`), keeping your existing entries:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@lidtop/opencode-later"]
}
```

**Where it runs.** The server side keeps the list and its settings in the OpenCode server's plugin storage and gives the agent its [tools](#agent-tools); the sidebar and `/later` in the terminal show and change that list over plugin RPC (both parts use the ID `opcode-later`). Configure it where the server reads plugins (this config, or the remote server's), not in `cli.json`: a terminal-only install has no server side to ask, and `/later` says to add it to the server's plugins.

**One list.** Every terminal connected to the same server, and the agent in every project, shares one list and its settings. A change anywhere shows in every open sidebar and `/later` dialog right away.

## Use

Run `/later` or select **Later** in the command palette. It opens a dialog with three tabs: **Later** (active items, in order), **History** (completed items, newest first), and **Settings**.

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `tab` / `shift+tab` | Switch tabs |
| `↑` / `↓`, `j` / `k` | Move selection |
| `enter` or `space` | Later: close the dialog, paste the item into the prompt, and complete it. History: restore the item |
| `a` | Add an item |
| `e` | Edit the selected item |
| `c` | Complete an active item, or restore a completed one |
| `d` | Delete permanently, after confirmation |
| `J` / `K` | Move an active item down / up |
| `/` | Search the tab's items |
| `r` | Refresh now |
| `esc` | Leave the search box, clear the search, then close |

**`enter` pastes an item into the prompt and marks it complete. It never submits the prompt or runs anything.** The text is inserted with normal paste behavior; existing prompt text is kept. Clicking an item does the same as `enter`.

Adding, editing, and deleting open OpenCode's own prompt in place of the dialog, which comes back on the same tab when you answer or cancel.

Duplicates are allowed. Items are trimmed and cannot be empty. Active numbers follow display order and are reassigned after removing or reordering. Restoring an item appends it to the active list. Nothing is captured from sessions automatically.

The sidebar lists the first active items, 5 by default, and "+N more in /later" for the rest; click it to open the dialog. Change the count in **Settings** (3, 5, 10, 15, or 20). The section is omitted when there are no active items; the plugin never forces the sidebar open. Changes from another terminal or the agent's tools appear automatically. Edits, completions, deletes, and pastes of an item that changed elsewhere are rejected rather than applied to a newer version. While the server can't read the stored list, `/later` says so and changes are refused, rather than starting an empty list over it; it tries again on its own.

### Paste limitations

Paste-and-complete works only when `/later` was opened over home or a session. It closes the dialog, then waits up to one second for the prompt's paste command to be ready; if that times out, the destination changes, the plugin unloads, or the item changes while waiting, nothing is pasted or completed.

OpenCode V2 has no prompt-text setter or paste acknowledgement, so the item is marked complete after the paste is dispatched, not after anything runs. Review the prompt before submitting it yourself. This is not an exclusive task queue: two clients can still paste the same item.

### Desktop

In OpenCode Desktop, Later is a side panel tab: open it from the **+** menu before the side panel tabs (it shows the active count), select **Later** in the command palette, or run `/later` to toggle it. Add items in the field at the top. Each active item has **Use** and a menu to edit, move up or down, complete, or delete it (after confirmation); **Show history** lists completed items to restore, edit, or delete. While the list has items, a "N for later" pill above the prompt lists them too.

**Use**, and picking a row in the pill, inserts the item into the prompt, focuses it, and marks the item complete. **It never submits the prompt.** An item that changed elsewhere since the list was read is not inserted; one that changes before it is completed stays active, and a toast says so. The desktop app follows the same list as every terminal, live, on the app's own server; while that server can't read the list, the tab says why.

## Agent tools

When the server side is loaded (an `opencode.json(c)` entry), the agent can manage the list when you ask, for example "add a Later item to bump the SDK" or "complete the Later item about docs":

| Tool | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `later_list` | Lists active items with their IDs, and completed ones on request |
| `later_add` | Adds an item to the end of the list |
| `later_edit` | Replaces an item's text, moves an active item to history, or restores a completed one to the end of the list |
| `later_delete` | Deletes an item permanently, **after you approve it** in OpenCode's permission prompt, which shows the item's text |

Adding and editing don't ask: an edit's result in the transcript includes the previous text, and a completed item can be restored. Deleting asks unless your permission rules already allow or deny `later_delete`. If the item changes while you decide, it is not deleted. Changes show up in an open `/later` dialog and the sidebar right away.

To stop the agent using them, set **Agent tools** to off in `/later` **Settings**. Sessions created after that don't get the tools. Older sessions keep them listed, so their requests stay the same and keep hitting the provider's prompt cache, but every call is refused. Turning the tools back on asks first: it adds them to every open session's request, so each one's next message misses the prompt cache once. The setting is shared by every terminal on the server and applies from the next request, without a restart.

## Data and privacy

The server's plugin storage keeps the item text you enter, IDs, order, timestamps, a revision counter, the sidebar item count, and, while agent tools are off, when they were turned off. It collects no session or project metadata, but item text can contain anything you type, and it is sent to the terminals connected to the server. Nothing else is sent anywhere.

Earlier versions kept the list in `opencode-later/later.sqlite` in the terminal's OpenCode state directory (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode`, or `~/.local/state/opencode`), or a custom `database` path. That list is not carried over: re-add the items you want to keep, then you can delete the file. The `database` option is gone.

## Replacing opencode-later

Its SQLite list is not imported, as above. Remove the old entry and install this package instead. Do not run both: they share `/later` and the sidebar.

## Development

From the repository root:

```sh
mise exec -- bun test plugins/later/test
mise exec -- bun run typecheck
mise run dev later
```

The build bundles the private `@opcode/core`, `@opcode/tabs`, and `@opcode/ui` workspaces into the package; OpenCode, OpenTUI, and Solid stay external.

# @lidtop/opencode-later

## 0.4.0

### Minor Changes

- 3b19c6f: Add an OpenCode Desktop part: a Later side panel tab (add, use, edit, reorder, complete, delete, and history), a launcher in the side panel's + menu with the active count, `/later` to toggle the tab, and a "N for later" pill above the prompt. Using an item inserts it into the prompt without submitting and completes it, unless it changed elsewhere first. It follows the same server-owned list as every terminal.
- 62c9603: Require OpenCode 2.2.0 and OpenTUI 0.7.

## 0.3.2

### Patch Changes

- 5ccffe8: Shared code moved into helpers every plugin bundles: the refresh schedule now also works outside the terminal, and there are new helpers for state shared by a server's projects, RPC contracts and handlers, and following a server's state. For Context, Feed, Later, and Media nothing changes. In Cost, Review, Snippets, and Sessions, a call the terminal aborted is no longer reported as a failure. In Sessions, every project open on a server now shares one search index connection and one writer per database file, rather than possibly one per project.
- 23e2ac6: Later now keeps its list on the OpenCode server, so every terminal connected to it and the agent in every project share one list and its settings, and a change anywhere shows in every sidebar and `/later` dialog right away. With a remote server, the agent's tools now change the list in your sidebar rather than a separate one on that machine. Configure the plugin where the server reads plugins (`opencode.json(c)`, not `cli.json`). The `database` option is gone: the list lives in the server's plugin storage. The list saved by earlier versions is not carried over; re-add the items you want to keep, then you can delete `opencode-later/later.sqlite` in the terminal's OpenCode state directory.
- e91635a: Shared code that Feed and GH PR Status use moved into helpers every plugin bundles: the minute clock that ages views, and sending changes to the server in order while showing them at once. Nothing changes for any plugin.

## 0.3.1

### Patch Changes

- e5df44d: The README opens with a short demo video.

## 0.3.0

### Minor Changes

- 889f494: The agent can now edit a Later item's text and restore a completed item, not only complete one: `later_edit` replaces `later_complete`. Edits don't ask, and the result in the transcript includes the previous text.
- e85fab8: `/later` is now a dialog in the format of `/feed` and `/ghpr`, with Later, History, and Settings tabs, search, and the same keys; `c` completes or restores an item, and `enter` closes the dialog and pastes the item into the prompt. The sidebar is quieter, lists 5 items by default (3 to 20 in Settings), and points to `/later` for the rest. When Later's server side is loaded, the agent can list, add, and complete Later items, and delete one after you approve it.
- e945860: Add an **Agent tools** setting to `/later` Settings, on by default. Turned off, sessions created afterward don't get the Later tools, and older sessions keep them listed (so their prompt cache still applies) but every call is refused. Turning them back on asks first, because each open session's next message then misses the prompt cache once.

### Patch Changes

- f27f920: `/later` cards start an item's text beside its number, with the age on the same line, and wrap long text under itself rather than under the number. History cards do the same beside their check mark.
- 76fed78: Show the Later sidebar's item numbers in the text color, with the items' text still muted.
- bb097fd: Require OpenCode 2.1.3 or newer.
- 1708674: Move Later's prompt paste helper into the shared UI package so Snippets can reuse it. No behavior changes.
- 44bad65: The Pull requests and Feeds sidebar sections show their refresh countdown beside the title instead of on a line of their own. Those sections and Agents no longer add a line saying there's nothing to show; they show just the title.

## 0.2.3

### Patch Changes

- 439c23e: Tag the package with the `opencode` and `opencode-plugin` npm keywords so plugin directories such as OpenDock can list it.
- 61dcef7: Later and Feed now place their sidebar sections below the ones OpenCode and other plugins add, so GH PR Status's Pull requests comes first. Between themselves, Later and Feed keep the order they're configured in.

## 0.2.2

### Patch Changes

- a8e520d: Standardize the package READMEs: install with `opencode plugin add` first, show screenshots, and use the same sections and wording across every plugin.

## 0.2.1

### Patch Changes

- e6b5093: Context no longer lets missing, negative, or non-finite provider usage values corrupt its token totals. History pagination, live-event reconnection, and usage normalization now behave consistently across plugins, and Cost always closes its ledger on unload. Errors with an empty message now show a readable fallback instead of a blank notification.
- 6eaeb52: Context and Cost now share one coalesced refresh from the bundled core utilities. Cost dashboard reads time out after 30 seconds instead of blocking later refreshes, and refresh-failure warnings in both stay visible until a retry succeeds. Later and Sessions only rebuild against the updated shared core.
- 5dfbfa9: Reordering now works in legacy lists whose items share the same stored position.
- 7a9d63d: Completing or deleting an item in another client no longer makes pending edits, deletions, completions, or pastes of other items fail as "changed elsewhere".
- a6e153f: A Later dialog that is replaced or dismissed without answering no longer leaves `/later` and its actions disabled.
- 1ae9d93: Create new Cost and Later databases owner-only (0600 files in a 0700 directory) before SQLite writes to them, as Sessions already did; existing database permissions are left unchanged. All plugins now share one XDG state-path resolver.
- e70e939: Measure and truncate labels with the host renderer's width method in every plugin, so Cost project, model, and warning labels no longer overflow with wide characters such as CJK or emoji. Cost, Later, and Sessions keyboard hints with a matching command are now clickable, and all views take their colors from the shared theme palette.

## 0.2.0

### Minor Changes

- 805bb55: Publish independently versioned OpenCode V2 plugins with bundled private helpers and terminal extensions.

### Patch Changes

- 8f1a01b: Balance theme colors: use normal foreground for page/dialog titles and shortcut keys, muted labels and neutral borders, accent hues for sections/charts, and interactive hues for values. Preserve the theme's contrasting selection foreground/background pair.
- 572b6e9: Restore consistent theme-aware colors for headings, borders, metrics, keyboard hints, charts, and statuses. Follow live light/dark theme changes and preserve dialog and selection colors.
